title: Visual run — the round record
note: ONE ITEM PER RUN. A run is a visual being worked toward acceptance; each ROUND of that run is its own append-only record on item `<run>.r<n>` (round 1 = `<run>.r1`), so the whole run reconstructs in order — /api/reviews is latest-per-reviewer, which would collapse rounds if they shared one item. Round verdict: {round, prompt, model, references[urls], candidates[{url, model, seed?, flags[{name,state:pass|flag|unverifiable}]}], pick|null, keep, fix, reject_reasons{index:[tags]}, fixed[], constraints[{name,text}], constraints_from (the prompt text those constraints were extracted from — present only when a lane extracted them; when it differs from `prompt` the operator has rewritten the prompt and the constraints are STALE: shown struck through and never sent to the check), advice{model,why}|null, decision: continue|accepted|parked|abandoned|null, at}; a flag may also carry note and by:'check'|'you'. The mini-worker files each generate-image manifest TWICE: on the bare `<run>` item (newest batch only — latest-per-reviewer overwrites it, which is what the cheap 20s poll reads) and on `<run>.gen.r<n>`, its own item per round, which is what keeps an earlier round's candidates readable at all. Each manifest image carries `url` (the vendor's, EPHEMERAL — 404 within hours), `drive_path` (durable, but a filesystem path no browser can fetch) and `durable_url` (the platform blob copy the bench renders from; added 2026-08-20). The AI lane files its results here too, on their own items: `<run>.prompt.r<n>` (write-prompt / rewrite-prompt) and `<run>.check.r<n>` (check-candidates), reviewer 'mini-worker' — separate items so they never collapse into the round record. Written by /v/<person>/the editor-ai (the the editor-ai-gen bench, EAG-N1; called roundworks until 2026-08-20, and that path still redirects). Known runs are listed in the items_file; open_items is on because both round ids and new runs are created by the bench, not by editing the index.
